scenes.title: Introduction
scenes.summary: Mr. Steven Knott hires the investigators to examine the Corbitt House in 1920s Boston after the Macario tragedy made it impossible to rent.
scenes.read_aloud: It is 1920 in Boston. Mr. Steven Knott, a landlord with a problem property, meets you with the keys and a retainer. The old Corbitt House has a violent reputation after the Macario family fled or collapsed into illness and madness. Knott wants the truth found and the house made rentable again. He gives you the address, keys, and $20 in advance, then waits to hear how you intend to begin the investigation.
scenes.gm_notes: Keep Mr. Knott mundane and anxious about money. He can confirm he recently inherited the property, cannot rent or sell it, and expects research before a risky visit. Do not expose the Keeper secret.

links.reason: Newspaper research can reveal the house history.

Court and police files can reveal the 1912 raid.
Neighbors may remember recent tenants and local rumors.

scenes.title: The Boston Globe
scenes.summary: The newspaper morgue can reveal the house has a long pattern of violent accidents, illness, suicide, and the Macario case.
scenes.read_aloud: The Boston Globe offices smell of ink, paper dust, and hot machinery. Staff can point you toward the basement clippings morgue, but the files are not open to casual visitors; an editor named Arty Wilmot controls access.
scenes.gm_notes: To access the clippings files, choose Charm/Persuade/Intimidate/Fast Talk according to player approach; Regular difficulty. On success, Ruth Blake takes them to the dusty morgue and Handout 2 becomes obvious by street address. On failure, Arty refuses; pushed failure should escalate beyond simple refusal.

links.reason: Follow up older property references at the library.
Civil records may predate surviving newspaper files.
The investigators can visit the house.

checks.failure: Arty denies access; pushed failure escalates

scenes.title: The Central Library
scenes.summary: Library research can reveal the house was built in 1835, bought by Walter Corbitt, litigated over his behavior, and tied to a contested basement burial.
scenes.read_aloud: The Central Library is quiet, formal, and full of old catalogues. The Corbitt House trail is not in one neat place; it will take careful half-day blocks of research to bring useful records together.
scenes.gm_notes: Each half-day of research asks for Library Use. For each success, reveal handouts 3-6 in order. If research exceeds a day, Mr. Knott checks in and presses for progress.

links.reason: The executor/church trail points toward civil records.
The chapel records may require higher court or police access.
The investigators can visit the house.

scenes.title: Hall of Records
scenes.summary: Civil records reveal Corbitt’s executor was Reverend Michael Thomas of the Chapel of Contemplation; church records note the chapel closure in 1912.
scenes.read_aloud: At the Hall of Records, bound registers and civil files sit behind clerks and indexes. The name Corbitt leads toward an executor, a church, and a closure date that does not feel ordinary.
scenes.gm_notes: Ask for Library Use. On success reveal Handout 7. Courteous clerk or Law can point toward county/commonwealth/federal courts and Central Police Station for serious-crime records.

links.reason: Serious-crime and police records may hold the missing chapel raid file.
The Chapel of Contemplation can be investigated directly.
The investigators can visit the house.

checks.success: reveal executor and Chapel of Contemplation connection

scenes.title: Higher Courts and Central Police Station
scenes.summary: Restricted records reveal a secret 1912 raid on the Chapel of Contemplation, deaths, missing autopsy detail, released cultists, official interference, and Michael Thomas’s conviction and escape.
scenes.read_aloud: Court and police records are less welcoming than public archives. Clerks, officers, and locked files make this a social or professional access problem before it becomes a research problem.
scenes.gm_notes: Access requires Law, Credit Rating 75+, Persuade, Charm, or Fast Talk as justified by roleplay. On success reveal Handout 8. On pushed failure, consequences can include police antipathy, threat, shakedown, or a bribe trap.

links.reason: The police file makes the chapel a concrete lead.
The investigators can visit the house.

scenes.title: The Neighborhood
scenes.summary: Neighbors near the Corbitt House can provide rumors and firsthand color about the house and the Macario family.
scenes.read_aloud: The streets around the Corbitt House carry the ordinary noise of Boston, but doors close a little faster when the address is mentioned. Some residents remember the Macarios; some would rather not talk.
scenes.gm_notes: Roleplay questioning neighbors. Mr. Dooley is a useful local contact. Use social skills only when pressure, credibility, or deception matters; success should produce concrete rumor or firsthand detail.

links.reason: Macario family testimony can be followed at the sanitarium.
The investigators can visit the house.

scenes.title: Roxbury Sanitarium
scenes.summary: The surviving Macario testimony points to something active in the house and may suggest Corbitt can be killed with his own dagger.
scenes.read_aloud: Roxbury Sanitarium is sterile, controlled, and sad. The Macario name opens a narrow path to a damaged witness, but whatever happened in the Corbitt House has not left him whole.
scenes.gm_notes: Vittorio Macario is unstable and frightened. Handle with care. If the investigators build enough trust or read his reactions, reveal that he fears the house and may understand that Corbitt can be killed with his own dagger.

links.reason: The dagger clue points toward the house basement and hidden threat.
The investigators can visit the house.

scenes.title: The Chapel of Contemplation
scenes.summary: The ruined chapel can yield occult records, the symbol handout, and the decisive clue that Walter Corbitt was buried in the basement of his house.
scenes.read_aloud: The Chapel of Contemplation is a ruin with a bad history and newer signs of disturbance. Dust, collapsed masonry, and a few surviving records make the place feel abandoned rather than empty.
scenes.gm_notes: Searching the cabinet can reveal old records. Handout 9 is the symbol. A key record states Corbitt was buried in the basement of his house in accordance with his wishes. Treat that as a concrete clue, not flavor.

links.reason: The burial clue points to the basement.
The investigators can visit the house.

data.obvious_clue: Walter Corbitt was buried in his house basement.

scenes.title: The Old Corbitt Place
scenes.summary: The investigators arrive at the old house; exterior entry and initial inspection set the frame for room exploration.
scenes.read_aloud: The Corbitt House waits behind its old address with the tired look of a place that has been explained away too many times. The keys fit. The windows are still, the air around the threshold stale.
scenes.gm_notes: Let players inspect entrances, windows, neighbors, or go inside. Do not force an option list. Keep hidden basement truth unrevealed until found through play.

links.reason: Entering the house leads to the ground floor.
The surrounding neighborhood can still be canvassed.

scenes.title: Corbitt House: Ground Floor
scenes.summary: Ground-floor rooms establish the derelict house, possible diaries/books, doors, kitchen, storage, and access toward upper floor or basement.
scenes.read_aloud: Inside, the house smells of old plaster, dust, and trapped damp. Everyday rooms have gone stale: furniture under grime, corners gone dark, and the sense that small noises carry too far.
scenes.gm_notes: Adjudicate room-by-room inspection. Searching can produce mundane details and any source-backed papers/books from rooms. Let player movement decide whether they go upstairs or down.

links.reason: Stairs lead up to the bedrooms.
A basement stair/door leads downward.
The exterior remains accessible.

section_path: Corbitt House Keeper Version / lower rooms

scenes.title: Corbitt House: Upper Floor
scenes.summary: Upper-floor bedrooms include Macario family spaces and the dangerous animated bed event.
scenes.read_aloud: Upstairs, the bedrooms still hold traces of a family interrupted: small beds, religious items, stale bedding, and a silence that makes every floorboard answer back.
scenes.gm_notes: If the bed attack triggers, ask Spot Hidden if appropriate, then Dodge to avoid being hit/thrown; seeing impossible movement requires SAN 0/1 or 1/1D4 as source notes indicate. Keep window positioning clear and impartial.

links.reason: The stairs return to the ground floor.
The investigation can move downward.

hazards.sanity: 1 point or 1D4 depending failure as source notes

scenes.title: Corbitt House: The Basement
scenes.summary: The basement contains a dangerous stair/door, the floating magical dagger, storage spaces, rats, and the concealed path to Corbitt’s lair.
scenes.read_aloud: The basement air is colder and wetter. Rough boards, old bins, and a dark under-space make the room feel less like storage than concealment.
scenes.gm_notes: Resolve dangerous descent with DEX/Climb when warranted. The floating dagger uses Corbitt’s POW and source rules; seeing it attack calls for SAN 1/1D4. Breaking/removing boards reveals crawl space, rats, and the carved Chapel clue; the inner wall can lead to Corbitt’s hiding place.

links.reason: Breaking through the hidden wall reveals Corbitt’s hiding place.
The stairs return upward.

scenes.title: Corbitt’s Hidden Lair
scenes.summary: The hidden room contains Corbitt’s undead body, papers, final confrontation, Sanity loss, combat, possible Dominate, Flesh Ward, and victory/failure outcomes.
scenes.read_aloud: Beyond the broken wall is a fouler space. On a pallet lies a tall, wasted figure, wood-dry and hairless, with a chain at its neck and a sweet rotten smell in the air. Curled papers sit on a small table in the corner.
scenes.gm_notes: When Corbitt rises, call for SAN 1/1D8. He has STR 90, CON 115, SIZ 55, INT 80, POW 90, DEX 35, APP 05, EDU 80, HP 16, MP 18, Fighting 50%, Dodge 17%, Flesh Ward armor 2D6 already cast, Dominate variant, floating dagger. If reduced to 0 HP he crumbles. If stabbed with his own dagger he quickly turns to ash regardless of spells. Victory pays fee plus bonus and grants 1D6 SAN.

links.reason: If Corbitt is destroyed or the investigators withdraw/fail, resolve the ending.

opponent.armor: Flesh Ward 2D6, depletes by damage blocked

scenes.title: Conclusion
scenes.summary: If Corbitt is destroyed, Knott pays promptly and each participating investigator gains 1D6 SAN; failure can leave Knott dead and police suspicion on the investigators.
scenes.gm_notes: Use source ending conditions. Do not declare a win without resolving Corbitt or a credible alternative. If investigators knowingly leave the threat active, report consequences honestly.

module_specific_rules.summary: Library/location research consumes half-day blocks and reveals handouts on success; failures can cost time rather than halt play.
Grabbing the floating dagger is a Fighting maneuver opposed by Corbitt POW; creative protection may grant a bonus die.

module_specific_rules.summary: If investigators wrest control of Corbitt’s dagger and stab him with it, he turns to ash regardless of spells.

scene_facts.text: It is 1920 in Boston and Mr. Knott has hired the investigators to examine the Corbitt House.
The investigation can progress through archives, witnesses, chapel records, and then the house itself.
The decisive hidden threat is tied to the house basement, but that fact should only be exposed through clues or play.

pressure_items.text: Knott pays by the day and wants the matter resolved before the property loses more value.
pressure_items.consequence_hint: If research drags on, Knott checks in and presses for action.

pressure_items.text: Corbitt can react to intruders inside the house through frightening phenomena and attacks.
pressure_items.consequence_hint: Unsafe exploration can trigger supernatural hazards.

affordance_items.description: inspect rooms, doors, floors, and hidden spaces
fight, flee, restrain, or improvise protection when supernatural hazards attack

risk_items.text: Do not reveal Keeper-only truth before player-visible clues justify it.
Physical harm and Sanity loss are possible in the house.
If the investigators falsely report the house safe, Knott may die and police suspicion can follow.

npc_advice.advice_text: Research first if you think it will help, but I need this house made safe and respectable again.
npc_advice.bias_or_goal: Wants a profitable resolution quickly and may minimize danger.
